Subject: Isolation validation runbook — operator scenarios & evidence pack

Hi Ethan,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our procurement RFP we need a short packet that demonstrates how Redwood will operate in our VPC/offline mode. Specifically we are trying to validate: 

- Operator access scenarios (initial provisioning, emergency break-glass, decommission) and role separation.
- KMS/HSM workflow when the control-plane is offline and how key material is protected during operator maintenance.
- Sample telemetry / audit-log schema and retention policy for offline deployments (we need to see an example log line with redacted identifiers).
- SLA failover behaviour when a dedicated pool is isolated or an operator needs to take systems offline.

Can you send: 1) a runbook (play-by-play) for the operator workflows, 2) an operator credential matrix, and 3) any sample audit-log and KMS integration artifacts you can share (redacted as needed)?

We need this evidence for our security committee by COB Friday (2026-08-06). Let us know if that timeline is feasible.

Best,
Melissa

Hi team — attaching the redacted evidence pack per your asks. Highlights below, and I added inline answers to your numbered items. Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_runbook_evidence (read-only link)

Attachments included:
- isolation-runbook-v1-redacted.pdf (redacted runbook; includes provisioning, emergency break-glass, decommission, and operator drills)
- operator-credential-matrix.xlsx (roles, approval paths, and credential rotation cadence)
- telemetry-data-map.csv (schema mapping)
- kms-integration-snippet.txt (anonymized envelope-wrapping sequence and config snippet)
- audit-log-sample.txt (synthetic, redacted log lines)

Responses to SecOps questions: 
1) Log snippet: included in audit-log-sample.txt — synthetic lines with timestamp, event=kms:encrypt, key_handle=KEY-REDACTED-1234, operator_id=OP_RED_001, resource=runtime-01.
2) HSM offline attestations: Yes — we support HSM-backed key material with an offline attestation flow. When offline, the runtime enforces a signed attestation token (generated during provisioning) and logs key-use events locally; those events are replayed to the control plane when connectivity is restored. Statement included in kms-integration-snippet.txt.
3) SLA failover behaviour: Deterministic routing is documented in the runbook: in-flight requests at the moment of isolation are: 
   - short-running (<250ms) tokenized requests: attempted to finish locally (best-effort),
   - streaming/generation requests: server returns a structured 503 with a retry-after and an optional client-side continuation token to resume after failover,
   - policy: we never silently route to a different customer-bound runtime; fallback is only to a pre-agreed, compatible model variant in the same tenancy. Full decision matrix is on page 14 of the runbook.

We can run the 30-minute tabletop on Tue 2026-08-10 16:00 ET — I will send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Action items:
- Marissa: produce 3-minute ops sim (in progress).
- Irene: confirm retention phrasing (90/365) and update runbook appendix (Irene, please add final text).
- Ethan: upload and send invite (this message).

If you need any additional snippets or direct log extracts (synthetic), tell me which format your audit team prefers (JSON lines / CSV).
